47971-field-book-of-western-wild-flowers.creator: Margaret Armstrong
47971-field-book-of-western-wild-flowers.description: A book by Margaret Armstrong. hundreds of flowers are to be found; many kinds of hardy plants brighten the salty margins of the sea cliffs, or bloom at the edge of the snow on rocky mountain peaks, while quantities of humble, everyday flowers border our country roadsides or tint the hills and meadows with lavish color.

arxiv-1501-03811.title: The Problem Of Grue Isn’t
arxiv-1501-03811.creator: William M. Briggs
arxiv-1501-03811.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by William M. Briggs. The so-called problem of grue was introduced by Nelson Goodman in 1954 [ 2 ] as a “riddle” about induction, a riddle which has been widely thought to cast doubt on the validity and rationality of induction. That unnecessary doubt in turn is partly responsible for the reluctance to adopt the view that probability is part of logic: for that view see, e.g., [ 1 , 4 , 7 ] .

arxiv-2101-05456.title: Self-supervised learning for segmentation
arxiv-2101-05456.creator: Abhinav Dhere, Jayanthi Sivaswamy
arxiv-2101-05456.description: Abstract Self-supervised learning is emerging as an effective substitute for transfer learning from large datasets. In this work, we use kidney segmentation to explore this idea. The anatomical asymmetry of kidneys is leveraged to define an effective proxy task for kidney segmentation via self-supervised learning.

arxiv-2209-02137.title: There is no complete numerical invariant for smooth conjugacy of circle diffeomorphisms
arxiv-2209-02137.creator: Philipp Kunde
arxiv-2209-02137.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Philipp Kunde. Classical results by Poincaré and Denjoy show that two orientation-preserving C 2 C^{2} diffeomorphisms of the circle are topologically conjugate if and only if they have the same rotation number. We show that there is no possibility of getting such a complete numerical Borel invariant for the conjugacy relation of orientation-preserving circle diffeomorphisms by homeomorphisms with higher degree of regularity.

arxiv-2501-10304.title: Magnetic properties of the zigzag ladder compound SrTb 2 O 4
arxiv-2501-10304.creator: F. Orlandi, M. Ciomaga Hatnean, D.A. Mayoh, J.P. Tidey, S.X.M. Riberolles, G. Balakrishnan, P. Manuel, D.D. Khalyavin, H.C. Walker, M.D. Le, B. Ouladdiaf, A. R. Wildes, N. Qureshi, O.A. Petrenko
arxiv-2501-10304.description: Abstract We report on the properties of SrTb 2 ​ O 4 \rm SrTb_{2}O_{4} , a frustrated zigzag ladder antiferromagnet, studied by single crystal neutron diffraction (with polarised neutrons in zero field and unpolarised neutrons in an applied magnetic field), as well as by neutron spectroscopy on a polycrystalline sample.

arxiv-2502-05608.title: Closing the Responsibility Gap in AI-based Network Management: An Intelligent Audit System Approach
arxiv-2502-05608.creator: Emanuel Figetakis 1 , and Ahmed Refaey 1
arxiv-2502-05608.description: Abstract Existing network paradigms have achieved lower downtime as well as a higher Quality of Experience (QoE) through the use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based network management tools. These AI management systems, allow for automatic responses to changes in network conditions, lowering operation costs for operators, and improving overall performance.

arxiv-2502-07255.title: Beyond Confidence: Adaptive Abstention in Dual-Threshold Conformal Prediction for Autonomous System Perception
arxiv-2502-07255.creator: Divake Kumar, Nastaran Darabi, Sina Tayebati, and Amit Ranjan Trivedi
arxiv-2502-07255.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Divake Kumar, Nastaran Darabi, Sina Tayebati, and Amit Ranjan Trivedi. Safety-critical perception systems require both reliable uncertainty quantification and principled abstention mechanisms to maintain safety under diverse operational conditions. We present a novel dual-threshold conformalization framework that provides statistically-guaranteed uncertainty estimates while enabling selective prediction in high-risk scenarios. Our approach uniquely combines a conformal threshold ensuring valid prediction sets with an abstention threshold optimized through ROC analysis, providing distribution-free coverage guarantees ( ≥ 1 − α \geq 1-\alpha ) while identifying unreliable predictions.

arxiv-2504-07352.title: Interesting Deformed q q -Series Involving The Central Fibonomial Coefficient
arxiv-2504-07352.creator: Ronald Orozco López
arxiv-2504-07352.description: Abstract In this paper, we will obtain a variety of interesting q q -series containing central q q -binomial coefficients. Our approach is based on manipulating deformed basic hypergeometric series. Keywords: Deformed q -series; q -series; central q -binomial coefficients; Lehmer series; generalized Fibonacci polynomials Mathematics Subject Classification: 05A30, 11B83, 33D15.

arxiv-2510-19569.title: Implications of f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) gravity on late-time cosmic structure growth through a complete description of density perturbations
arxiv-2510-19569.creator: Miguel Barroso Varela, Álvaro de la Cruz-Dombriz
arxiv-2510-19569.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Miguel Barroso Varela, Álvaro de la Cruz-Dombriz. We provide insight about the full form of the equations for matter density perturbations and the scalar Bardeen metric potentials in general f ⁡ ( R ) f(R) theories of gravity. When considering viable modifications to the standard Λ \Lambda CDM background, the full scale-dependent equations for the metric perturbations are provided and are shown to match the ones obtained with the quasistatic approximation.

arxiv-2511-17445.title: Origin of large topological Hall effect in the EuCd 2 Sb 2 antiferromagnet
arxiv-2511-17445.creator: Faheem Gul, Orest Pavlosiuk, Tetiana Romanova, Dariusz Kaczorowski, Piotr Wiśniewski
arxiv-2511-17445.description: Abstract We study the origin of large topological Hall effect in the single-crystalline EuCd 2 Sb 2 , which orders antiferromagnetically at the Néel temperature T N = 7.4 T_{\rm N}=7.4 K. Measurements of magnetoresistance and Hall resistivity disclose anomalies that evolve with temperature and magnetic field, closely tracking the magnetization process.

arxiv-2511-18563.title: Object-centric Task Representation and Transfer using Diffused Orientation Fields
arxiv-2511-18563.creator: Cem Bilaloglu, Tobias Löw, Sylvain Calinon
arxiv-2511-18563.description: Abstract Curved objects pose a fundamental challenge for skill transfer in robotics: unlike planar surfaces, they do not admit a global reference frame. As a result, task-relevant directions such as “toward” or “along” the surface vary with position and geometry, making object-centric tasks difficult to transfer across shapes.

arxiv-2512-06592.title: On fine-tuning Boltz-2 for protein-protein affinity prediction
arxiv-2512-06592.creator: James King, Lewis Cornwall, Andrei Cristian Nica, James Day, Aaron Sim
arxiv-2512-06592.description: Abstract Accurate prediction of protein–protein binding affinity is vital for understanding molecular interactions and designing therapeutics. We adapt Boltz-2, a state-of-the-art structure-based protein–ligand affinity predictor, for protein–protein affinity regression and evaluate it on two datasets, TCR3d and PPB-affinity. Despite high structural accuracy, Boltz-2-PPI underperforms relative to sequence-based alternatives in both small- and larger-scale data regimes.

pmc-11398757.creator: Lauren Gates-Tanzer, Elena Millesi, Aparna Vijayasekaran, Christin Harless
pmc-11398757.description: Background:In 2020, the American Board of Plastic Surgeons announced an update in the leave policy for plastic surgery trainees, extending personal leave to 12 weeks without delay in graduation. pmc-12590639.title: Chronic headache disorders as a threat to brain health among employees of a city office in the Tokyo metropolitan area
pmc-12590639.creator: Mamoru Shibata, Toshihiko Shimizu, Ryo Takemura, Fumihiko Sakai
pmc-12590639.description: BackgroundChronic headache disorders, especially migraine, are known to cause considerable loss of productivity and negatively affect brain health in the workplace. The present study aims to clarify how common chronic headache disorders are and how much productivity loss they are causing within administrative bodies.

pmc-12631158.title: Loss of the RNA Binding Protein HuR in Early Murine Limb Mesenchyme Does Not Affect Development but Leads to Impaired Bone Homeostasis in Adulthood
pmc-12631158.creator: Shijian Fu, Kirsty A Johnson, Phaedra Winstanley‐Zarach, Ufuk Ersoy, Elena Adlmanninger, Benjamin T McDermott, Craig Keenan, Aphrodite Vasilaki, Ioannis Kanakis, Peter I Milner, Rob J van’t Hof, Dimitris Kontoyiannis, George Bou‐Gharios, David A Turner, Simon R Tew
pmc-12631158.description: In this study, we examined how a critical posttranscriptional regulator, the RNA‐binding protein HuR (gene name Elavl1), contributes to the development and maintenance of limb skeletal tissue. Using the Prx1‐Cre knockout model, we examined the effect of germline knockout (Elavl1KO) and limb mesenchyme‐specific knockout (MSC‐Elavl1KO) of HuR on limb development.

pmc-13079715.title: Revealing the hidden third dimension of point defects in two-dimensional MXenes
pmc-13079715.creator: Grace Guinan, Michelle A Smeaton, Brian C Wyatt, Steven Goldy, Hilary Egan, Andrew Glaws, Garritt J Tucker, Babak Anasori, Steven R Spurgeon
pmc-13079715.description: Point defects govern many important functional properties of two-dimensional (2D) materials. However, resolving the three-dimensional (3D) arrangement of these defects in multi-layer 2D materials remains a fundamental challenge, hindering rational defect engineering. Here, we overcome this limitation using an artificial intelligence-guided electron microscopy workflow to map the 3D topology and clustering of atomic vacancies in Ti3C2TX MXene.

pmc-13086432.title: Comparison of serum vitamin D level and vitamin D receptor gene FokI polymorphism in leprosy patients with and without trophic ulcers: A case-control study
pmc-13086432.creator: Paulus Anthony Halim, Sondang P. Sirait, Eliza Miranda, Yulia Ariani, Wresti Indriatmi, Hok Bing Thio, Stuart D. Blacksell, Mohammad Jokar, Stuart D. Blacksell, Mohammad Jokar, Stuart D. Blacksell, Mohammad Jokar, Stuart D. Blacksell, Mohammad Jokar
pmc-13086432.description: BackgroundAlterations in the vitamin D axis have been implicated in chronic wounds, but their role in leprosy-related trophic ulcers (TU) is unclear. This study compared serum vitamin D levels and VDR FokI (rs2228570) polymorphism between leprosy patients with and without TU, assessed their association with ulcer presence, and examined the correlation between vitamin D levels and ulcer severity.
